name: SunFounder GalaxyRVR
description: A 6-wheel Mars-rover-styled kit from SunFounder with genuine rocker-bogie suspension — the same working geometry NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers use, not just a cosmetic 6-wheel arrangement. Unlike SunFounder's own PiCar-X, this runs on an Arduino Uno-class board with a bolted-on ESP32-CAM for WiFi FPV streaming, not a Raspberry Pi — skid-steered like a real rover, with no onboard computer vision.

sourcing: Verified against SunFounder's official GalaxyRVR product page and full course documentation (including the rocker-bogie mechanism lesson and the Mars-rover-history lesson); the sunfounder/galaxy-rvr GitHub repository and its firmware source, license, and star/commit activity; independent reviews from CNX Software, The Gadgeteer, and kevsrobots.com; an independent developer's blog covering firmware-flashing friction and the Arduino Uno's memory limitations; and Amazon, AliExpress, and eBay listings for pricing and availability. Flagged as uncertain: real-world solar-panel charging performance, which is a genuine spec but was not independently measured by any reviewer found in this research; and current stock availability, since SunFounder's own store showed it sold out at points during research.

pricing.summary: GalaxyRVR lists at $129.99 direct from SunFounder — about 44% more than PiCar-X's ~$89.99 base price. It's sold through SunFounder's own store (shown sold out at points during research, suggesting intermittent stock issues), Amazon, AliExpress, and eBay, with no evidence of a crowdfunding campaign; it appears to have launched as a direct catalog product like SunFounder's other kits.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: GalaxyRVR's firmware is genuinely open source (GPL-3.0) but far less mature than SunFounder's own PiCar-X codebase, with roughly 15 stars versus picar-x's stronger community traction. SunFounder's claimed roughly 7.2-hour full solar charge time hasn't been independently measured by any reviewer in this research, so treat that figure as unverified rather than disproven.
